components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Journey of water through Earth's atmosphere, land, and oceans

components.title: The Endless Cycle of Life
components.subtitle: Discover how every drop of water on Earth has been here for billions of years, moving in a continuous loop.

blocks.title: 1. Evaporation
blocks.text: The Sun heats up water in rivers, lakes, and oceans, causing it to change from a liquid into water vapor and rise into the sky.

blocks.title: 2. Condensation
blocks.text: As water vapor rises high into the cooler air, it cools down and turns back into tiny liquid water droplets, forming clouds.

blocks.title: 3. Precipitation
blocks.text: When the water droplets in clouds become too heavy, they fall back to the Earth as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: Tracing a Single Raindrop
components.Body: Let's trace a molecule of water starting from the Pacific Ocean. It absorbs solar heat (`Evaporation`), floats up into the atmosphere where it cools and joins a cumulus cloud (`Condensation`), and eventually drops onto a mountain peak as fresh snow (`Precipitation`).
components.code: Ocean (Liquid) -> Vapor -> Cloud Droplet -> Snow Crystal
components.code_caption: Phase transitions during a single atmospheric journey.
components.takeaway: Water never leaves the Earth; it only changes its physical state and location.

quiz_data.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapor?
quiz_data.explanation: Evaporation is the process where liquid water absorbs heat and turns into gas or vapor.

quiz_data.question: Which phase comes right before precipitation in clouds?
quiz_data.explanation: Condensation happens when water vapor cools down and turns back into liquid droplets, forming clouds.

quiz_data.question: Where does most of the precipitated water eventually end up?
quiz_data.explanation: Oceans and major water bodies collect the vast majority of surface runoff and precipitation.
